- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward — overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows strong upward bias in the middle to late forecast horizon (days 15–30), often failing to account for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the first 5–10 days, leading to lagged corrections.
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections after spikes — often holds high prices longer than observed.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the 30-day forecast, especially when recent history shows consolidation or decline.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shocks (e.g., ETS auction events) in the short-term horizon.
